explanation: Use TYPE = SERVICE for an organization user that represents a service or application operating without human interaction.
reasoning: Snowflake introduced PERSON and SERVICE organization user types. PERSON remains the default when TYPE is omitted; SERVICE is intended for non-human applications and services.

distractor_analysis.why_wrong: PERSON represents a human organization user and is the default if TYPE is omitted.
LEGACY_SERVICE is not one of the supported organization user types described in the release.
APPLICATION_ROLE is an access-control object concept, not an organization user TYPE value.

exam_trap: Do not confuse an organization user's identity type with roles used to grant privileges.
code_example: CREATE ORGANIZATION USER app_identity TYPE = SERVICE;

explanation: PERIOD represents an anchored temporal range using half-open semantics: the beginning bound is inclusive and the ending bound is exclusive.
reasoning: Snowflake distinguishes PERIOD from interval types. An interval is a duration without a fixed position on a timeline, whereas PERIOD identifies a specific range such as an employment or validity window.

distractor_analysis.why_wrong: An unanchored duration describes an interval concept, not PERIOD.
PERIOD is a first-class temporal data type, not a semi-structured object.
PERIOD can use DATE, TIME, or TIMESTAMP bounds and is not merely an account-time-zone timestamp.

exam_trap: The key distinction is anchored range versus duration, plus [begin, end) boundary semantics.

explanation: Existing semantic views and verified queries can carry over because Cortex Agents uses Cortex Analyst as its structured-data tool.
reasoning: Snowflake's transition guidance says teams do not need to rebuild the semantic layer. Cortex Agents preserves the structured-data path while adding orchestration, tool calling, conversation threads, and unstructured retrieval through Cortex Search.

distractor_analysis.why_wrong: Snowflake explicitly states semantic views carry over unchanged.
The transition does not require uninstalling Cortex Analyst; the REST API remains available.
Cortex Agents can work across structured and unstructured data rather than only unstructured sources.

exam_trap: Transitioning to Cortex Agents changes invocation and orchestration, not the underlying semantic model for structured analytics.

sources.title: Snowflake recommends transitioning from Cortex Analyst to Cortex Agents

explanation: The Spark job capability in Code Bundles is built on Snowpark Connect.
reasoning: The September 2026 Code Bundles preview added Spark batch jobs and stated that Spark support is built on Snowpark Connect, enabling existing Scala, Java, or Python Spark applications to run on Snowflake compute without re-platforming.

distractor_analysis.why_wrong: Snowpipe is an ingestion capability and does not provide the Spark execution layer described in the release.
Secure Data Sharing governs data collaboration, not Spark execution.
External Functions are unrelated to the Snowpark Connect foundation used for Spark jobs.

exam_trap: Do not conflate Snowpark Connect for Spark compatibility with Snowpark's ingestion or sharing features.

explanation: Use the retry_upgrade remote app operation to retry a failed Snowflake Native App upgrade.
reasoning: Remote app operations let providers perform on-demand operations on consumer apps. Supported examples in the GA release include run_sql, retry_upgrade, disable, and enable. Restricted operations such as run_sql require consumer consent.

distractor_analysis.why_wrong: rebuild_package is not listed as a remote app operation in the release.
force_listing is not a remote app operation for recovering an app upgrade.
reset_release_channel is not the documented operation for retrying a failed upgrade.

exam_trap: Separate application package/version concepts from the specific remote operation used to recover an installed app upgrade.

sources.title: Remote app operations for Snowflake Native Apps (General availability)

explanation: Per-user quotas are the Snowflake capability for enforcing configurable credit limits at individual-user granularity across supported warehouse and AI usage domains.
reasoning: The GA release allows quota administrators to set daily and monthly per-user credit limits, notify users at thresholds, target all users or subsets, and block AI access when AI quota limits are reached.

distractor_analysis.why_wrong: Search Optimization Service improves query lookup performance rather than imposing user spend limits.
Fail-safe is a data-recovery service and is unrelated to user-level credit governance.
Replication groups move or replicate account objects and data; they do not cap individual user spend.

exam_trap: Resource governance for ML/AI includes cost controls; do not assume warehouse resource monitors are the only cost-governance mechanism.

explanation: WITH GRANT OPTION allows the recipient role to grant the received account role or database role onward to other roles.
reasoning: Snowflake's October 2026 update added WITH GRANT OPTION for role-to-role grants. REVOKE GRANT OPTION FOR can later remove only the onward-grant ability while leaving the role grant itself in place.

distractor_analysis.why_wrong: OWNERSHIP is an object privilege concept and is not the clause used to delegate role grants.
Managed access controls privilege-grant administration within schemas; it does not enable onward role grants.
COPY CURRENT GRANTS is not the documented clause for role grant delegation.

exam_trap: WITH GRANT OPTION here applies to grants from one role to another role; grants to users do not support the clause.
code_example: GRANT ROLE ANALYST_BASE TO ROLE ANALYST_LEAD WITH GRANT OPTION;

sources.title: WITH GRANT OPTION for role grants

explanation: The Workday Data Cloud Zerocopy Connector mounts the Workday catalog as a catalog-linked database so Snowflake can query the source directly without ETL, replication, or moving the data out of Workday.
reasoning: Each Workday namespace maps to a schema and each Workday table maps to a table. Snowflake contacts Workday on each SELECT, so the source stays current and Workday remains the system of record.

distractor_analysis.why_wrong: Export-and-load pipelines move data and introduce copy/latency, contrary to the zero-copy requirement.
A clone would be a Snowflake-side copy and would not provide live zero-copy access to Workday as system of record.
A materialized view over an internal stage requires staged data and therefore does not satisfy the zero-copy architecture.

exam_trap: Zero-copy here means federated-style direct access through a catalog-linked database, not merely avoiding a traditional ETL tool.

sources.title: Zero-copy integration for Workday Data Cloud (General availability)

explanation: SNOWFLAKE.ACCOUNT_USAGE.STREAMS provides an account-level row for each stream and includes metadata such as source object, base tables, mode, and staleness.
reasoning: The 10.35 release introduced this Account Usage view specifically to improve visibility into streams across an account, which is useful for monitoring data engineering pipelines and stale stream conditions.

distractor_analysis.why_wrong: STAGES inventories stage-related metadata, not stream source, mode, and staleness properties.
LOAD_HISTORY focuses on load operations rather than an inventory of stream objects.
QUERY_ATTRIBUTION_HISTORY concerns query cost attribution and does not provide the stream inventory described.

exam_trap: Know the distinction between object inventory/health metadata and operation-history views.

explanation: Cortex AI Gateway is Snowflake's governed entry point for AI inference traffic, with model access governance, request tracing, usage reporting, and cost controls.
reasoning: The preview provides standard API formats, a per-gateway trace table, AI_GATEWAY_USAGE_HISTORY for usage attribution, Snowsight monitoring, budget integration, and compatibility with per-user quotas. It governs the traffic path but does not grant model entitlements that users do not already have.

distractor_analysis.why_wrong: Snowpipe Streaming is an ingestion capability rather than an AI model governance endpoint.
Fail-safe is for disaster recovery of Snowflake-managed data and is unrelated to AI inference governance.
Database replication is for data/account continuity and does not provide agent/model request tracing or inference routing.

exam_trap: The gateway does not expand model permissions; underlying model access controls still apply.

explanation: Use WEEKLY as the cycle value when configuring a weekly per-user quota limit.
reasoning: The September 2026 update added a weekly cycle alongside daily and monthly cycles. The weekly cycle follows the ISO week and resets Monday at 00:00 UTC.

distractor_analysis.why_wrong: WEEK is not the documented cycle literal for SET_PER_USER_LIMIT.
ISO_WEEKLY is not the documented cycle literal even though the schedule follows ISO-week timing.
SEVEN_DAY is not supported as the named weekly quota cycle in the release.

exam_trap: Remember the API literal WEEKLY and separately remember the ISO-week reset behavior.

explanation: Snowflake PERIOD values use half-open range semantics: the beginning bound is included and the ending bound is excluded.
reasoning: A PERIOD identifies a specific anchored temporal range. The [begin, end) convention makes adjacent temporal windows easier to model without double-counting a boundary instant.

distractor_analysis.why_wrong: The ending bound is not inclusive.
The beginning bound is inclusive, not exclusive.
The beginning bound is included in the PERIOD.

exam_trap: Temporal range boundary semantics are easy to reverse; memorize PERIOD as [begin, end).
